column2: A client struggles with figures. Which question checks their understanding of an early exit charge?
column3: What would you receive if you left today?
column4: Can I show you the fee table again?
column5: Would a printed copy of the terms help?
column6: Shall I ask someone else to join us?
column7: Asking the client to explain the effect reveals how they understood the charge. A different format may help them learn but tells the adviser little about their present understanding.

column2: A designer is layering information about charges. Which feature belongs on the opening screen?
column3: Key costs with links to detail
column4: Worked figures for a specialist case
column6: Definitions of technical charging terms
column7: Layering puts the costs that matter to the immediate decision upfront. Specialist calculations and definitions can sit in the detail that follows.

column2: Which question establishes the time horizon for a client's investment objective?
column3: When will you need this money?
column4: How often do you receive a payslip?
column5: How long have you owned shares?
column6: When was your pension last reviewed?
column7: The investment horizon runs until the client expects to use the money. Time already spent investing helps establish experience instead.

column2: Which fact best measures whether a client can afford losses in their savings portfolio?
column5: Years spent investing through a workplace plan
column6: Preferred balance of bonds and shares
column7: Capacity for loss depends on the financial consequences of a fall. A client's confidence during a downturn is evidence about willingness to take risk.

column2: Using TEXAS, what follows thanking a client who has disclosed a health condition?
column3: Explain how the information will be used
column4: Explore how the condition affects them
column6: Check the basis for recording the details
column7: In TEXAS, the adviser explains the use of the information before the model's data-processing check, further questions and signposting.

column2: An insistent client receives further advice about their chosen transaction. What happens to the original recommendation?
column3: It stands as a separate conclusion
column4: It becomes advice on the new transaction
column6: It becomes the client's preferred alternative
column7: The FCA expects the adviser to distinguish the new advice from the original conclusion. Agreeing to advise further does not retrospectively change the first recommendation.

column2: A customer discloses a condition that affects concentration. Which note best supports future appointments?
column3: Short meetings help the client stay engaged
column4: The client disclosed a condition in March
column5: An adviser discussed an adjustment by phone
column6: A follow-up appointment took place on Tuesday
column7: Recording what helps the client allows the next adviser to deliver the adjustment. Dates or contact history alone give little practical guidance.

column2: A client follows written explanations well but misses details on calls. Which adjustment matches this need?
column5: Arrange a later call with more breaks
column6: Book a shorter series of voice calls
column7: The difficulty concerns the channel. Adjusting a call's length or timing can help with fatigue, while a written channel uses the client's preferred way of receiving information.

column2: Which FCA principle applies most directly to safeguarding investments held on a customer's behalf?
column6: Customers' relationships of trust
column7: A firm responsible for client assets must protect them adequately. Financial prudence concerns the firm's own financial resources.

column2: Which FCA principle addresses whether a firm's systems cope with threats to its business?
column6: Conflicts of interest
column7: Management and control concerns how the firm organises its affairs and manages risk. Skill, care and diligence covers the standard with which it conducts its business.

column2: Who should approve a firm's regular assessment of how well it delivers Consumer Duty outcomes?
column6: Its compliance monitoring team
column7: The board or equivalent governing body reviews and approves the assessment. Compliance staff may supply the analysis that informs that judgement.

column2: A branch changes how bonuses are earned. Which FCA driver of culture does this chiefly affect?
column3: How people are managed and rewarded
column4: How directors set the firm's purpose
column5: How the risk committee reports breaches
column6: How leaders communicate their priorities
column7: Pay influences what staff have an incentive to do. In the FCA framework this falls under the people driver.

column2: What belongs in an individual senior manager's statement of responsibilities?
column4: Skills required to qualify for the post
column6: Scores from their last conduct assessment
column7: The statement describes the manager's personal accountabilities. A job specification describes the skills required of someone doing the work.

column2: A manager delegates daily reconciliations. Which action demonstrates oversight of how the deputy performs them?
column4: Prepare the monthly rota for the team
column6: Update the job description for the role
column7: Reviewing and questioning unresolved differences tests how the delegated work is being discharged. Resourcing and job design help assign the task.

column2: Who issues the certificate for an employee performing an FCA certification function?
column6: The firm's statutory auditor
column7: The firm assesses fitness and propriety for the function and issues the certificate. Regulatory approval follows a different process for senior management functions.

column2: An adviser has persistent unpaid judgment debts. Which element of fitness and propriety is most directly relevant?
column6: Product knowledge
column7: The assessment considers a person's financial standing as well as conduct and competence. The existence of debt calls for assessment in context.

column2: Which evidence best supports the competence assessment of a newly promoted advice supervisor?
column4: Length of previous service in sales
column5: Attendance at the annual conduct briefing
column6: Number of clients in the former portfolio
column7: Competence needs to be assessed against the particular role. A past sales record gives limited evidence of the ability to supervise other advisers.

column2: Which cultural driver concerns how a firm detects recurring harm and tackles its underlying cause?
column6: Leadership example
column7: The firm's controls and processes should bring poor outcomes to light and support corrective action. Rewards influence individual behaviour through a different driver.

column2: When does Principle 11 require a firm to disclose an issue to the FCA?
column3: When the FCA would reasonably expect notice
column4: When a customer files a formal complaint
column5: When external auditors quantify the total loss
column6: When the FCA begins a supervisory visit
column7: The firm's disclosure obligation depends on what the regulator would reasonably expect to learn. A supervisory visit is not a necessary trigger.

column2: Small policies carry the same flat fee as large ones. How should the board examine fair value?
column6: Compare margins by distribution channel
column7: A flat fee can affect groups differently. Breaking down outcomes by policy size can reveal poor value that an average would conceal.

column2: A supplier invites an adviser to a modest dinner during a tender. What does the hospitality provision address?
column6: Accuracy of the tender specification
column7: The CII Code includes the appearance of an improper obligation. Modest cost alone does not settle how the invitation could reasonably be seen.

column2: A broker offers a reward to induce a buyer to breach procurement duties. When can bribery first occur?
column6: When the reward is paid
column7: An offer made with the necessary intent can itself complete the offence under the Bribery Act. The buyer need not accept it or award the contract.

column2: Two clients competing for one business seek advice from the same adviser. What kind of conflict arises?
column4: Between a client and the adviser's finances
column6: Between professional development and sales
column7: Separate duties can conflict when acting for one client would prejudice the other. The adviser need not have a personal financial stake.

column2: A prospect gives an adviser personal figures before declining a quote. Which obligation survives that decision?
column6: Monitoring the cost of ongoing advice
column7: The Code protects confidential information supplied by prospective clients. The other activities arise from providing an ongoing service.

column2: Which record best tests a fund's claim that it excludes fossil fuel producers?
column6: Industry engagement report
column7: Holdings reveal whether the fund owns the excluded businesses. Voting and engagement report how the fund uses its influence as an investor.

column2: An individual adviser holds Chartered status. What must a firm establish before using the corporate designation?
column3: Its own entitlement to the title
column6: Its staff's current training budgets
column7: The CII distinguishes status held by an individual from the status of an organisation. One person's award does not establish the firm's entitlement.

column2: A sales agent bribes a buyer to win work for a firm. What supports its statutory defence?
column4: Prompt dismissal of the agent responsible
column5: Voluntary repayment of the contract profit
column6: A directors' resolution to end the contract
column7: Under section 7 of the Bribery Act, the firm can defend a failure-to-prevent charge by proving it had adequate procedures at the time. Actions taken after discovery do not alone establish that defence.

column2: Which evidence tests whether customers understand a charge, rather than whether they have seen it?
column4: Their visits to the charges page
column5: Their receipt of the annual notice
column6: Their downloads of the tariff sheet
column7: A customer who can apply the tariff demonstrates understanding of the charge. Page visits establish exposure to the information.

column2: Which measure would show whether a revised withdrawal service gives clients faster access to cash?
column5: Time from account opening to first request
column6: Time from payment to statement issue
column7: End-to-end payment time measures when the client actually receives funds. A prompt acknowledgement can precede a lengthy delay.

column2: A review finds an adviser gave specialist advice beyond their abilities. Which aspect of service failed?
column6: Handling complaints through a written process
column7: Personal competence limits the work an adviser can undertake. Accurate records and a clear fee explanation do not establish the ability to advise on a specialist product.

column2: The CII Code allows an exception to declining conflicted work. Which source can establish that exception?
column6: A provider's distribution agreement
column7: CII members should refuse the work unless the regulator expressly permits acting in the circumstances. An agreement among the parties alone does not establish the exception.

column2: Which process can the CII initiate under its own Code following misconduct by a member?
column4: A review of the firm's FCA permission
column6: A market abuse prosecution
column7: The CII acts through its disciplinary process. A breach of its membership standards can be investigated independently of statutory regulatory or criminal proceedings.
